figures.finding: A person domiciled in Pakistan attains majority on completing eighteen; a minor for whose person or property a court has appointed a guardian (or whose property a Court of Wards superintends) only at twenty-one. Marriage, dower, divorce and adoption are outside the Act.
figures.applies: Majority Act 1875 ss. 2-4, Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice).

sources.said: Subject as aforesaid, every other person domiciled 1[Pakistan] shall be deemed to have attained his majority when he shall have completed his age of eighteen years and not before.

figures.finding: Only a person of the age of majority is competent to contract in Pakistan, so a minor's contract for creative work doesn't bind him; no statute read sets aside a minor's earnings, and nothing read distinguishes writing or directing.

sources.said: 11. Who are competent to contract. Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

figures.finding: Under the federal Employment of Children Act 1991 (in force for the Islamabad Capital Territory; the provinces have enacted their own laws since the 18th Amendment, not read), a child (under fourteen) is barred only from the scheduled occupations and processes (which list work in cinemas, not film production); elsewhere a child may work no more than three hours without an hour's rest, seven hours a day including rest and waiting, never between 19:00 and 08:00, no overtime, not for two establishments the same day, with a weekly holiday. No permit exists; the rules reach any child employed, actor, writer or director alike (reading).

value.scheduledBar: Part I occupations and Part II processes (includes work in cinemas)

figures.applies: Employment of Children Act 1991 ss. 2, 3, 6-8 and Schedule, Pakistan Code.

sources.said: “child” means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age; ... 3. Prohibition on Employment. ___ No child shall be employed or permitted to work in any of the occupations set forth in Part I of the Schedule or in any workshop wherein any of the processes set forth in Part II of that Schedule is carried on: ... (2) The period of work on each day shall be so fixed that no period shall exceed three hours and that no child shall work for more than three hours before he has an interval of at least one hour for rest. (3) The period of work of a child shall be so arranged that inclusive of the interval for rest, under sub-section (2), it shall not exceed seven hours, including the time spent in waiting for work on any day. (4) No child shall be permitted or required to work between 7.00 p.m. to 8.00 a.m. (5) No child shall be required or permitted to work overtime. ... (27) Work in cinemas, mini cinemas and cyber clubs.
